messages:
lucy: Heads-up — customer ACME reported a big p95/p99 jump after our canary runtime rollout (v4.2.5). p95 went ~80ms -> ~420ms, p99 ~220ms -> ~1.2s starting ~15:30 UTC. No CPU/GPU increase in their tenant, but auth/token latency in traces looks bad. Link to short trace: https://short.link/trace-abc

jon: seeing the same in env metrics — auth token fetches from auth-service spiked ~8x for canary pods, and KV cache miss rate + retry loops increased. No obvious model compile regressions.

alex: possible coldstart to KMS/HSM connections per pod? If token cache TTL got shorter in 4.2.5 we could be hitting remote KMS more often which kills tail latency. Any deploy notes? :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: deployed runtime:v4.2.5 -> canary (subset=5%) at 4790015800 commit=3f9de2f.

pri: model serving traces look normal, CPU and GPU time per request steady. The extra time is entirely in auth/token and the first HTTP hop to auth.

lucy: support customer provided quick repro (curl):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <client-token>" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
They also gave a sanitized log: 
```
[15:31:04] request start
[15:31:04] auth: cache miss -> calling auth-service (latency 420ms)
[15:31:04] retry 1 to auth-service (latency 410ms)
[15:31:05] runtime: start model inference (100ms)
[15:31:05] total latency 1.1s
```

jon: quick triage checklist: 1) verify auth token TTL change in config diff, 2) check KMS latency and connection reuse, 3) see if circuit-breakers started firing causing retries. I'm going to run a canary-level flame graph and capture auth-service call traces.

lucy: customer also saw increased 429s and billing-related retries — calls retried bumped token usage which might inflate billable units. Mel from CS is in loop.

mel-cs: confirmed customer asked for temporary mitigation and credit evaluation. We'll hold credits until postmortem. For now they want performance restored ASAP.

alex: I can repro locally by spinning up canary config: the auth client in 4.2.5 recreates TLS context per token request (we changed the HTTP client factory). That explains the extra ~300-400ms per call on cold paths.

jon: OK mitigation options: A) rollback canary to v4.2.4 (fast, removes regression), B) hotpatch auth client to reuse TLS context, C) temporarily bump token cache TTL so we hit KMS less. We should do rollback to stop customer impact and buy time for a proper patch.

ryan-oncall: rolling back canary now to v4.2.4 (5% -> revert). Patching rollout controller...

deploy-bot: rollback initiated to runtime:v4.2.4 at 4790016018 by ryan-oncall.

ryan-oncall: rollback completed at 4790016030. Monitoring p95/p99...

jon: initial numbers look good — p95 dropped to ~92ms and p99 to ~240ms for the affected cohort within ~6m after rollback. Auth fetch rate back to baseline. :thumbsup:

lucy: told customer we've rolled back canary and are investigating root cause; offered apologies and asked if they want temporary credits. Mel will handle follow-up.

alex: action items: (1) PR to revert the HTTP client factory change that recreated TLS contexts (owner: alex, due: EOD), (2) add unit/integration test to cover auth client reuse (owner: jon), (3) add canary gating metric for auth-service call-rate+latency threshold (owner: pri), (4) add instrumentation to track KMS/HSM handshake latencies per pod (owner: infra), (5) support to review billing impact and customer credit (owner: mel).

jon: also recommend adding a small synthetic test that does token fetches at canary deployment time to catch cold-start regressions before rollout.

lucy: I'll open an incident ticket and link this thread. Follow-up postmortem please include timeline, config diffs (4.2.4 -> 4.2.5), and billing impact estimate.

mel-cs: keeping customer updated — they appreciated quick rollback. Will provide billing info and ask if they want extended monitoring window.

alex: postmortem note — this looks like a regression introduced to an auth helper lib; low risk change but high tail impact. We'll be conservative with client-factory changes going forward.

jon: if anyone sees related spikes in other canaries, ping this thread. Good catch by support.

lucy: thanks everyone. closing loop once postmortem and credits decided. :white_check_mark:
